ety.text: Hawaiian ʻaʻābor. English aa Borrowed from Hawaiian ʻaʻā.

senses.d: A form of lava flow associated with Hawaiian-type volcanoes, consisting of basaltic rock, usually dark-colored with a jagged and loose, clinkery surface. Compare pahoehoe.
ex: We...saw ‘pahoihoi’ or solid lava forming, and also ‘aa’ or clinkers.
Cooling and solidification frequently takes a different course [...] in lava flows, producing the clinker-like ‘aa’ lava.

grp.label: a form of lava flow associated with Hawaiian-type volcanoes
